Vide this common award, I shall decide two DAR (Detailed Accident Report) cases arising out of the same motor vehicular accident resulting into injuries to petitioner Amit Sahni (injured in MACT Dar - Suman Bishtania vs Badshah And Ors on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181945251/

sentences.text: The DARs have been treated as claim petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 for grant of compensation to the injured/ claimant.

2. Briefly stated the facts of the case as emerged from the FIR and DAR are that on 20.03.2021 at 11:00 a.m., the petitioners Amit Sahni and Suman Bishtania were going from Shahdara to Dilshad Garden Metro Station side in an e-rickshaw and when they reached near Petrol Pump, Jhilmil Metro Station, Delhi, all of a sudden, a DTC bus bearing registration no.DL1PD-3206, (in short "offending vehicle"), being driven by its driver at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner came and hit t h e e - r i c k s h a w f r o m b e h i n d , d u e t o w h i c h b o t h t h e p e t i t i o n e r s f e l l d o w n o n ________________________________________________________________________________ MACT nos. 324/2022 & 325/2022 2 of 14 Pages road and sustained injuries.
They were taken to GTB Hospital, Delhi, where their MLCs were prepared.
On the statement of one of the injured namely Amit Sahni, FIR no.94/2021, under sections 279/337 IPC was registered at PS GTB Enclave.

During investigation, it was found that the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1,
owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3 at the time of accident.
3. All the three respondents appeared and filed their written- statements.

3.1 In the written-statements filed on behalf of respondent nos.1 and 2, it is stated that they have been falsely implicated in this case and that no accident as alleged caused due to negligence of respondent no.1 who was having valid driving license.

3.2 Respondent no.3/ insurance company in its written-statement admitted that admitted that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it but contended that their liability is subject to compliance to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

4. Upon completion of pleadings of the parties, vide order dated 17.01.2023, following issues were framed:
(Re: injured Amit Sahni)
i).

Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 20.03.2021 at about 11:00 a.m., near Petrol Pump, Jhilmil Metro Station, within the jurisdiction of PS GTB Enclave, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no.

Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

My findings on the issues are as under:-

sentences.text: Issue no.1, being interlinked in both the cases, shall be decided here together by my common findings.
It is the settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.

However,
the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012,
Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530,
Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: On this issue, testimonies of both the petitioners who sustained injuries in the accident are most relevant to be discussed here.

PW1 Amit Sahni (in MACT 324/2022) testified that on 20.03.2021 at 11:00 a.m., he and co-passenger Suman Bishtania were going from Shahdara to Dilshad Garden Metro Station side in an e-rickshaw and when they reached near Petrol Pump, Jhilmil Metro Station, Delhi, all of a sudden, a DTC bus bearing registration no.DL1PD-3206, being driven by respondent no.1 at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner came and hit the e-rickshaw from behind, due to which both the petitioners fell down on road and sustained injuries. PW1 Suman Bishtania also deposed on the lines of PW1 Amit Sahni.
9. Both the witnesses (petitioners) were cross-
examined by learned counsel for the respondents.

I may note that the aspect of rash and negligent act of the respondent no.1 remained intact and that testimonies of eye-witnesses/ injured could not be shattered in any manner during their cross-examination and therefore, their testimonies have to be accepted on its face value itself.
Further, nothing else is available on record which may suggest any falsity in the oral testimony of petitioners.

10. Further, the ocular testimony of the petitioner(s) (in both the cases) is also corroborated by documentary evidence brought on record by way of DAR (Ex.PW1/D) comprising of MLCs of injured, site plan of place of accident, seizure memo of the offending and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle, FIR and the charge-sheet.

11. Furthermore, there is no challenge from the respondent no.1/ driver of the offending vehicle to t h e

o f

T h e ________________________________________________________________________________ MACT nos. 324/2022 & 325/2022 6 of 14 Pages respondent no.1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the testimony of the petitioners regarding the above accident and its manner but he preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the Dar - Suman Bishtania vs Badshah And Ors on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181945251/

sentences.text: During the course of final arguments, learned counsel for the respondents argued that there was delay of 20 days in registration of the FIR in this matter and secondly, mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle does not mention any fresh damages to it which indicates that offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in this case.
I have perused the DAR filed by the Investigating Officer in this case, which includes the FIR, charge-sheet and mechanical inspection report, etc.

I may note that though it is correct that FIR was lodged on 10.04.2021 i.e. 20 days after the date of accident which occurred on 20.03.2021 but it is evident from the record that information qua accident was received in the Police Station on the same day, which was reduced into writing by HC Chhote Lal vide DD no.49A dated 20.03.2021.

Besides that, as per charge- sheet and during cross-examination of the injured Amit Sahni (PW1), it came on record that since he was not well and was not in a proper condition to walk due to injuries and therefore, he could not visit the Police Station to lodge the FIR.

Petitioner further stated that later, he requested police personnel to visit his house and thereupon, Investigating Officer went his place to record his statement and thus, the F I R  
w a s

In these circumstances, I find that there is justifiable explanation for causing delay in registration of FIR.
13.

The another contention of respondents qua no fresh damages to the offending vehicle shown in mechanical inspection report, is concerned, I may observe that since it is a case of simple injury as per MLC of the petitioners and DAR, there was hardly any chance of visible damages on the offending vehicle and that is why no fresh damages could have been observed/ recorded during mechanical inspection of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the aforesaid pleas of the respondents, being not tenable in the eyes of law, are rejected.

14. It is not disputed that respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted in the criminal case by the police after detailed investigation and in a motor vehicle accident claim case, the contents of charge sheet are admissible in evidence and deemed to be correct under Rule 7 of Delhi Motor Accident Tribunal Rules, 2008, which support the version of petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
15.
Thus, the facts that FIR had been registered and charge sheet had also been filed against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.

Reliance is placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case titled as Shabina v.
Satvir & Ors. MAC. APP. 980/17 dated 24.01.2020, wherein Hon'ble Delhi High Court observed that in so far as FIR has been registered, criminal case has been initiated against driver of offending vehicle and vehicle was seized, the requirement of proving the preponderance of probability of a c c i d e n t h a v i n g b e e n c a u s e d b y r a s h a n d ________________________________________________________________________________ MACT nos. 324/2022 & 325/2022 8 of 14 Pages negligent driving of the offending vehicle has been established.

sentences.text: ON perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No. 955/2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle, (ii) Criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under Section 279/304-A IPC against the driver, (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
Hence, this contention of the counsel of the appellant also falls face down.
There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of driver."
16. Besides above, the MLC of both the petitioners which are part of DAR Ex.PW1/D prepared at GTB Hospital, reflects that they sustained simple injuries in RTA (road traffic accident).

Thus, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into simple injuries to the petitioner Amit Sahni and Suman Bishtania.
Issue no.1 in both the cases is, accordingly, decided in favour of petitioner(s).
ISSUE NO.2 18.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION (In Re: injured Amit Sahni) And (In Re: injured Suman Bishtania)

19 . Record shows that immediately after the accident, both the injured (petitioners herein) were t a k e n t o G T B H o s p i t a l , D e l h i , w h e r e t h e i r ________________________________________________________________________________ MACT nos
MLCs were prepared.

Injured Amit Sahni was medically examined vide MLC no. A/464D/19/2021 dated 20.03.2021 whereas injured Suman Bishtania was medically attended vide MLC no.A/4639/19/2021 dated 20.03.2021.
20.
As per MLC of injured Amit Sahni, he sustained lacerated wound of 3x3 cm on left knee with abrasions on right knee, left ankle and left elbow.
Attending doctor observed him to be conscious and fit for statement and the injuries sustained by him were opined to be simple in nature.

Further,
MLC of injured Suman Bishtania reveals that she suffered lacerated wound of 4x1 cm over left parietal region with complaints of pain in left elbow.
She was also conscious and fit for statement.
She was opined to have suffered simple injury.
21. It is evident from record that both the injured/ petitioners sustained simple injuries.

Further, I may note that except their MLCs, they did not place on record any medical bill or medical treatment document to show any expenses incurred on their medical treatment, conveyance, special diet and attendant charges, if any.

Thus, considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the opinion that interest of justice would be served if both the petitioners namely Amit Sahni and Suman Bishtania are awarded a lump sum compensation of Rs.20,000/- each towards pain and sufferings.
INTEREST ON AWARD 22.
Petitioners in both the cases shall also be entitled to interest @ 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove on record that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/ violated by insured, therefore, respondent no.3/ insurance company is held liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.

It is not disputed that respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted in the criminal case by the police after detailed investigation and in a motor vehicle accident claim case, the contents of charge sheet are admissible in evidence and deemed to be correct under Rule 7 of Delhi Motor Accident Tribunal Rules, 2008, which support the version of petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
15.
Thus, the facts that FIR had been registered and charge sheet had also been filed against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.
National Insurance Company Pvt. Ltd. v. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. (2008) 101 DRJ 645, wherein it was observed:
Thus, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into simple injuries to the petitioner Amit Sahni and Suman Bishtania.
Issue no.1 in both the cases is, accordingly, decided in favour of petitioner(s).
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
